memos.headline: S09 Remains the Standout Leader; Broad Weakness Elsewhere Warrants Caution on S05, S06, and S04
memos.body: I see a market where most names are trading below their 50-day means with RSIs in the low 40s, signaling a broad corrective phase. S09 is the clear outlier—up 30.4% over 12 weeks, sitting just 2.8% off its 52-week high, with massive +32% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks and RSI at a healthy 58.9. S05 and S06 are flashing near-oversold RSIs (34.8 and 35.9) with 4-week drawdowns of roughly -10% and -7% respectively, and both are underperforming SPY meaningfully on a 4-week basis. S04 is in a deep structural downtrend at -24.6% from its 52-week high and -15.6% below its 200-day mean, though the 4-week bounce of +3.9% and positive relative strength hint at a possible bottoming attempt. S07 had a brutal -8.3% week but retains a powerful longer-term trend (+56.6% over 26 weeks, +31.9% above 200d); I'd watch the 50-day mean closely—a decisive break below it would change my constructive view.

views.note: Dominant relative strength (+32% vs SPY 12w), near 52w highs with RSI 58.9—trend intact; would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~138).
Massive 26w gain of +56.6% and +31.9% above 200d, but sharp -8.3% weekly drop and RSI 40.1 suggest pullback risk; invalidated below ~660 (50d area).
RSI 34.8 is near oversold but 4w return of -9.9% and -9.1% relative to SPY show aggressive selling; no reason to step in until RSI stabilizes above 40.
Below both 50d (-7.0%) and 200d (-3.5%) means with RSI 35.9 and persistent negative relative strength; trend is clearly down.

Deep drawdown of -24.6% and well below 200d mean (-15.6%), but 4w bounce of +3.9% with improving relative strength (+4.7% vs SPY) could signal early bottoming; need a reclaim of 430 to turn constructive.
Sitting right at its 200d mean with +12.7% 12w relative strength vs SPY, but -8.1% last week is a sharp rejection; watching 150 as support.
Mild 4w bounce of +3.5% and near 200d mean, but -14.1% drawdown and RSI 42.4 leave it in no-man's land; need a break above the 50d to get interested.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Deliver Exceptional Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Red on Margin Collapse
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between durable, high-margin compounders and names where earnings power is deteriorating fast. S10 stands out with 73.2% YoY revenue growth, a 63.1% net margin, and only $8.47B in total debt—this is the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S04 is similarly impressive at a 47.3% net margin with net income up 59.5% YoY, though its $40.26B debt load warrants monitoring. On the other end, S02 posted near-zero net income ($0.01B) on $113.22B of revenue despite 12.3% top-line growth, meaning margin compression has essentially wiped out earnings; I cannot own that until I see operating leverage return. S09 is shrinking revenue (-1.3% YoY) while net income fell 14.6%, and its 7.9% net margin on $34.24B of debt leaves little cushion—I'd need to see a revenue inflection before getting constructive.

views.note: 73% revenue growth, 63% net margin, minimal leverage at $8.47B debt—best earnings quality in the universe; a deceleration in revenue growth below 30% would change my view.
47.3% net margin and 59.5% YoY net income growth demonstrate powerful operating leverage; I'd reassess if margins compress below 40%.
18% revenue growth, 30.3% net margin, and low debt of $14.79B make this a solid compounder; net income growth of 29.8% YoY confirms durable earnings.
Revenue of $143.76B and 29.3% net margin are solid, but $88.50B in total debt and only mid-teens growth temper enthusiasm relative to S10 and S04.
Largest revenue base at $213.39B but sub-10% net margin and only 5.9% net income growth suggest limited earnings upside without margin expansion.
28.4% net margin is respectable but net income declined 7% YoY and $435B in total debt (financial institution) makes the leverage profile hard to compare; need to see earnings stabilize.
19.4% net margin is decent but 1.5% revenue growth and -6.7% net income decline signal stagnation; would need reacceleration above mid-single-digit growth to get constructive.
18% revenue growth is encouraging but net income fell 13.9% YoY and 12.5% margin on $36.21B debt is thin; need to see margin recovery before committing.
Revenue declining 1.3% with net income down 14.6% and a thin 7.9% margin on $34.24B debt signals deteriorating earnings power; would reconsider only on a return to positive revenue growth.
Near-zero net income ($0.01B) on $113B revenue and $78B debt is a clear cash-flow compression story; 12.3% top-line growth is meaningless without margin recovery.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Slowing; Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth and Staples Over Banks
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in a late-stage easing cycle: the upper bound has fallen 75bp over 12 months to 3.75%, though the pace has slowed to just 25bp in the last three months, suggesting a pause is approaching. CPI is running at 2.4% y/y—still above target but not alarming—while unemployment has drifted up 30bp y/y to 4.3%, consistent with a mild slowdown rather than recession. The 10y yield at 4.15% is essentially flat over three months and the 2s10s spread at +56bp remains positively sloped, which tells me the market is pricing a soft landing with limited further easing. A hot February CPI print above 0.4% m/m or a surprise jump in unemployment above 4.5% would force me to revisit this benign-pause regime call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from a still-easing Fed and stable long rates; the regime favors quality growth over value.
Staples offer defensive carry in a mild-slowdown, late-easing environment with unemployment trending higher.
Cyclicals face mixed signals: easing supports activity but rising unemployment and slowing cut pace limit upside.
Banks face net-interest-margin compression as the front end falls faster than the long end, with the 2s10s spread flattening over three months.
Energy lacks a clear macro tailwind; soft demand backdrop from rising unemployment offsets any supply-side support.
Rate-sensitive sectors like real estate or utilities benefit from the cumulative 75bp of easing and stable 10y yields.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S02 and S04 Washouts May Be Bottoming While S07 and S01 Hold Positive Tone
memos.body: I am reading the event-driven price reactions across the universe to gauge where negative sentiment may have already been flushed and where positive tone could be crowded. S02 suffered a brutal -19.6% earnings-day drop on Jan 27, followed by two consecutive director departure/appointment 8-Ks in late Feb and early March—this cluster of management turnover after a massive selloff suggests the narrative is resetting, and the worst sentiment may be priced. S04 dropped -10.0% on its Jan 28 earnings release with no subsequent corrective filings, leaving negative tone dominant but potentially exhausted. On the positive side, S07 posted a clean +3.4% earnings reaction on Jan 29 with no negative follow-up filings, and S01 gained +2.6% on its Q2 results with supportive Reg FD disclosures bracketing the print. I have lower conviction on S06 and S10, both of which saw meaningful earnings-day declines (-4.2% and -5.5% respectively) accompanied by elevated filing activity that signals ongoing uncertainty rather than a clean washout.

views.note: Massive -19.6% earnings selloff likely over-discounted bad news; subsequent management changes hint at narrative reset that could turn tone positive.
The -10.0% earnings drop was severe but with no follow-up filings to anchor a recovery narrative, I lack conviction to go long yet.
Clean +3.4% earnings reaction with no subsequent negative filings keeps positive sentiment intact and uncluttered.
Positive +2.6% earnings reaction supported by bracketing Reg FD disclosures suggests constructive tone that has not yet become crowded.
Earnings-day -4.2% decline followed by heavy filing cadence including director changes and multiple Reg FD disclosures signals unresolved negative narrative.
Recent -5.5% earnings drop on Feb 25 is too fresh for sentiment to have bottomed; director turnover in January adds uncertainty.
The -5.6% earnings selloff was partially offset by a material definitive agreement filed Feb 27, but it is unclear if tone has fully turned.
Muted +0.5% earnings reaction and a routine shareholder vote filing generate no strong sentiment signal in either direction.

memos.headline: Surging Policy Uncertainty and Oil Prices Signal Structural Geopolitical Risk Repricing Across the Universe
memos.body: I am seeing a dramatic escalation in geopolitical and policy risk indicators: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has surged 64% over three months to 387.92, VIX is up 54% over the same period to 23.75, and WTI crude has spiked 34% to $80.88/bbl — a combination that historically accompanies sanctions escalation, supply-chain disruption, or major trade-policy shifts. High-yield spreads have widened only modestly (+15bp over 3m to 3.00%), suggesting credit markets have not yet fully priced the tail risk embedded in the volatility and uncertainty gauges. The flattening of the 10y-2y spread by 18bp in just one month adds a macro-slowdown overlay to the geopolitical picture. I have limited company-specific detail — the 8-K filings across S01, S02, S03, S05, S06, S07, and S09 are mostly Reg FD disclosures without granular content — so my conviction is moderate and tilted toward names with lower geopolitical exposure. A reversal in my view would require the EPU index falling below 300 and WTI retreating below $70, signaling de-escalation of whatever policy or conflict dynamic is driving these readings.

views.note: No company-specific filings to assess geopolitical exposure; elevated macro uncertainty warrants caution but no directional call.
Unusually high 8-K filing frequency (four filings in ~6 weeks) during a period of surging policy uncertainty suggests the company may be navigating material geopolitical or regulatory headwinds.
Two Reg FD disclosures in January with no further filings; policy uncertainty backdrop keeps me sidelined until content clarity improves.
Late-February 8-K with both Reg FD and Other Events items coincides with peak uncertainty readings; I need more detail before taking a directional stance.
Single 8-K in mid-February provides insufficient signal; the crude oil spike could be a tailwind or headwind depending on sector, which I cannot confirm.
No company-specific filings but the combination of 54% VIX surge and 34% oil spike in three months historically punishes names with energy-cost or supply-chain concentration risk.
Single early-January Reg FD filing predates the worst of the uncertainty spike; insufficient information to differentiate from the broader cautious stance.
One Reg FD disclosure in late January; no evidence of specific geopolitical exposure but macro backdrop warrants holding off.
